reason: EditScore shows a new pipeline working from start to finish. It has a human-agreement benchmark, a specialized reward model that beats open VLMs and matches proprietary ones, and controlled RL comparisons where off-the-shelf VLM rewards fail and EditScore improves OmniGen2 on two benchmarks, plus ablations on ensembling, score range and reward variance. SWE-Bench Pro is likely more significant as a resource, but the paper is thin as science. Its contamination resistance through GPL licensing is asserted rather than measured, two of three subsets are private, and it evaluates only one scaffold. Its reported numbers conflict between the text and tables (Sonnet 17.6 vs 16.3, GPT-4o 4.9 vs 3.9), and its failure-mode prose does not match Table 3.
